study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modeling of brain MRI data identifies small subcortical volumes and associations with cognitive function in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD)

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Quantify regional subcortical volume anomalies in youth with FASD using a normative MRI model; assess sensitivity/specificity of small volumes for group discrimination; examine associations between regional volumes and cognitive function.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests compared regional z-scores between FASD and comparison groups; percentages and sensitivity/specificity analyses for thresholds; Pearson correlations between regional volumes and cognitive measures (IQ, D-KEFS tasks) performed by group.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Youth with FASD showed more and larger-magnitude reductions in regional subcortical volumes than comparisons, especially in bilateral hippocampi and caudate; small-volume thresholds identified a substantial subset of FASD cases and volumes related to cognition within groups.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Across 7 bilateral subcortical ROIs, the FASD group had lower mean z-scores in 6/7 regions with largest effects in bilateral caudate and hippocampi (e.g., left hippocampus d≈0.85, right hippocampus d≈0.63, left caudate d≈0.85, right caudate d≈0.90; Table 2). Overall, 89% of FASD participants had ≥1 small subcortical volume vs 72% of comparisons. Using z ≤ -1.3, regions with highest relative sensitivity included bilateral putamen, bilateral hippocampi, right pallidum, and right accumbens (≈40–53% sensitivity; Table 3), with generally high specificities. Exploratory correlations showed positive associations between caudate volume and IQ/cognitive flexibility in FASD, and negative associations between putamen/pallidum volumes and IQ in comparisons.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Demonstrates use of a pre-trained normative tool (CentileBrain) to generate ROI-wise deviation scores and threshold-based summaries that may aid identification of neurodevelopmental anomalies in FASD.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Systematic shifts in z-scores relative to the normative reference likely due to acquisition/preprocessing differences (HCP pipelines, Siemens gradient corrections) and FreeSurfer version heterogeneity between study data (v6.0) and normative training datasets (≤5.3 or ≥7.1); no explicit harmonization to address such domain differences.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Single-site 3T Siemens Prisma acquisition with HCP-D-like sequences; processing via HCP Minimal Preprocessing Pipeline (v4.0.1) using FreeSurfer v6.0. QC included ENIGMA protocols, visual curation, Euler metric; exclusions: 3 comparison due to failed FreeSurfer, plus 5 (3 comparison, 2 FASD) for motion/outlier. Authors note potential domain shift vs multi-site CentileBrain norms (87 datasets; 37,407 brains).
